title: Prompts as code: versioned files pinned to a complete suite run
request: Treat prompts as code with tests. Keep each policy's system prompt and tool schemas in versioned files; record a hash of each next to the latest scripted-suite result; make rd-check fail when a prompt or schema changed and the suite has not been re-run for that hash; when a live baseline exists, print the change in score per case after a run. No prompt text is edited by a model.
spec: A change to a policy prompt, a tool schema or a validator rule must pass the scripted suite; the live results of the last release are the baseline to compare. Done when a test fails when a prompt file changes without its recorded hash being updated by the suite run.
plan: Find every prompt DCLab sends to a model: ten, as string constants in their modules (intern, home_agent, home_plan, synthetic_schema, parse_pattern, stage_critique, stage_explain, leakage_review, notebook_fixes, evidence_answer).

Move each into dclab_rnd/prompts/<name>.md, read with prompts.text(name); a number a prompt states becomes a placeholder filled from the module's constant; compare every prompt byte for byte before and after.
Write prompts.fingerprints() over the prompt files and each tool scope's schemas; store it with every scripted run (AEV-003); write tests/test_prompt_gate.py; make live runs compare with a baseline.
Run check-all and the review; fix four findings; rerun the suite (a failed run turned out to be the disk filling again); commit.

decisions.decision: The move must change no prompt: each module's text is compared byte for byte before and after.
decisions.why: A refactor of prompts that changes a word changes behaviour with no test noticing, the very risk the package removes.

decisions.decision: Only a complete scripted run (every policy on every case, no errors) stores the hashes.
decisions.why: Otherwise a partial run, or one where every case errors, satisfies the gate while the suite has not passed.

decisions.decision: The campaign tool's schema is hashed by its name, description and fields, not by pydantic's generated JSON schema.
decisions.why: The generated schema depends on the installed pydantic version, so the gate would flip between machines with no repository change.

decisions.decision: The gate asks for a rerun, not for the scores to hold.
decisions.why: A score drop after a prompt change is for a person to judge; the gate's job is to make sure the change was measured.

decisions.decision: A test keeps code from writing the prompt files.
decisions.why: People edit prompts; no tool or model may.

change: dclab_rnd/prompts/ with ten .md files and text(name) with placeholders checked for being filled; fingerprints() over the prompts, the project, draft, session and campaign tool schemas, and the workflow validator's rules (studio/graph.py); scripted runs store prompt_hashes only when complete; tests/test_prompt_gate.py names what changed and asks for make agent-eval; a live run compares with the last completed live result of the same model on the same cases, after its own result is written.

findings.defect: The gate accepted a partial or failing scripted run.
findings.scenario: Rename a required argument of a project tool so the standard policy errors on every case, then run the suite with --policy bad, or a full run whose results all have errors: the gate passed either way, because it checked only that some scripted file had the new hashes.
findings.cause: prompt_hashes were stored on every run, including policy subsets, and the runner always returned 0.
findings.fix: Hashes are stored only by a complete run (all three policies, every case, no errors), and the gate test fails when the latest scripted run is not complete.

findings.defect: The live baseline could be a run on different cases, so printed score changes meant nothing.
findings.scenario: The qwen baseline AEV-002 covers 2 cases x 2 repeats; the next full 20-case run would print 'leaks_caught 0.0 -> x' as if comparable; any smoke run would become the next baseline; a redefined case would be compared with its old table. Also, a baseline file without a summary raised KeyError before the paid result was written, losing it.
findings.cause: baseline() took the latest file for the model and ignored its case set, fingerprints and status; the comparison ran before writing.
findings.fix: The baseline is the last completed live result of the same model on the same cases with the same fingerprints; the comparison runs after the result is safely written; a smoke run is never a baseline.
findings.test: Baseline tests with mismatched case sets.

findings.defect: Validator rule changes were not part of the gate.
findings.scenario: Change a check in studio/graph.py, for example a gate rule: make rd-check stayed green without a suite rerun, though the package lists validator rules.
findings.cause: The fingerprint covered prompt files and tool schemas only.
findings.fix: The validator's rules are part of the fingerprint.
findings.test: The gate test; A5.2 and A6.1 later triggered it and reran the suite.

findings.defect: The campaign tool's hash depended on the installed pydantic version.
findings.scenario: A fresh environment or CI resolving another pydantic would produce a different JSON schema, failing the gate with no repository change.
findings.cause: The schema was generated by model_json_schema(), and pydantic was pinned only in the agent lock file.
findings.fix: The campaign schema is hashed by its name, description and fields.

findings.defect: The suite run failed with a directory error, so the gate failed for lack of a new result.
findings.scenario: Only 1.3 GB was free again; the rerun passed.
findings.cause: A full disk: direct test runs outside make do not get the per-command temporary folder cleanup, and scratch files had grown.
findings.fix: The space was found and freed and the suite rerun; no code change, since the failure was the machine, not the suite.

measurements.name: AEV-003, scripted suite rerun after moving the prompts
measurements.gate: The move changes no prompt (byte-identical), so the complete scripted run must give the same scorecard as AEV-001.
measurements.result: Same scores: standard 1 of 13 leaks, 1 false alarm in 20; audit 10 of 13, 3 in 20; bad 0 of 13, 20 of 20 unsafe moves refused. The reviewer also confirmed all ten prompts byte-identical and that one added trailing newline fails the gate.
measurements.next: For a prompt change the scripted rerun records it rather than tests it (no model is called); the live suite tests it.

outcome: Done: ten prompts are versioned files; their hashes, each tool scope's schemas and the validator's rules are pinned to a complete scripted run, and the test gate fails when any of them changed since. Open: the campaign's NOOA prompts, the research critics and the SFT corpus prompt stay in their modules. Four review findings fixed.
lessons: A regression gate must check that the run it trusts was complete and clean, not just that a file with the right hash exists.
Compare scores only between runs on the same cases with the same fingerprints; a smoke run is not a baseline.
Hash what you wrote, not what a library generates from it, or the gate depends on library versions.
